newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Siemens 96/97 loss at 845 mln.
newsitem.headline: India's Siemens 96/97 loss at 845 mln.

text.p: Siemens Ltd, Indian subsidiary of Germany's Siemens AG, on Friday said it reported a loss of 845 million rupees for 1996/97 compared to a net profit of 372 million in the previous year.
The turnover during the year rose by 10 percent to 11.66 billion rupees compared to 10.58 billion in the previous year, the company said.

"For the remaining six months of the extended financial year closing on September 30, 1997, Siemens is expecting a difficult operational environment which will make additional restructuring unavoidable," a company statement said.
Siemens attributed the loss to three main factors:
- the discontinuation of telecommunications operations which are being transferred to a new company Siemens Public Communication Networks Ltd,
- exceptional item in accounts during the year which includes the cost of restructuring of business operations, and
- the deterioration in operations of main businesses due to higher operational costs, lower capacity utilisation, higher interest and risk burden.
Earlier this year, Siemens AG officials said the firm was over-optimistic about Indian opportunities following liberalisation, and was restructuring its local operations.
